title: KS-590: Peter's four verify-by-hash disclosure questions: tighten or leave?
bluf: Peter (2026-10-06) asks you to rule four points, each changing what the cross-tenant test asserts: (1) certification.certifierOrganizationId survives scoping, so is an org UUID tenant-owned naming? (2) both chain-first branches skip scopeTenantFields; (3) rows with no tenancy info are never scrubbed; (4) the by-id path is never scoped. Anonymous verify stays a public 200 path (earlier ruling carried in the ticket). Tightening changes what verifiers, including Stuart's Platform S, see (production change once built); impact on S consumers unverified.

sources.quote: What's still missing is an answer to the four disclosure questions
Does an org UUID count as tenant-owned naming?
The by-id path selects no tenant_id, so it is never scoped
a test shouldn't settle them on its own

options.label: Strict: no tenant-owned naming incl. org UUID on all four paths (changes live verify)
options.detail: Agent build. Closes all four gaps. Verifiers incl. Platform S stop seeing the org id; confirm with Stuart first.

options.label: Fix gaps 2-4 (unscoped code paths) but allow the org UUID to be shown
options.detail: Smaller change; keeps the org id in verify output.
